1. # View Design: `mm::phys` (`src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs`)
2. 
3. > Phase output. Designs the abstract `View` that all later specs
4. > (`requires`/`ensures`) for `init`, `book_physical_memory_regions`, and
5. > `book_mmio_regions` will reference.
6. >
7. > Built **only** from `caller_analysis.md` and the body-removed public API
8. > (`body_removed_source.rs`), plus the **existing, do-not-modify** spec
9. > definitions (`byte_at_address`, `FrameAllocView`, `FrameAllocView::wf`,
10. > `frame_addr_of`, `View for Inner`, `Inner::inv`, `Inner::internal_inv`).
11. >
12. > Target functions in scope: `init`, `book_physical_memory_regions`,
13. > `book_mmio_regions`. (`test` is out of scope.)
14. 
15. ---
16. 
17. ## 1. Abstract Resource (from caller analysis)
18. 
19. `mm::phys` is, to its one caller (`kernel_vas::init`), the **boot-time
20. constructor of the machine's global physical-memory subsystem**. After
21. `init(..) -> Ok(())` the caller depends on a *world* in which:
22. 
23. 1. the **global frame allocator singleton is live** (initialized exactly once
24.    from the firmware bitmap) and internally consistent;
25. 2. every frame of every supplied *non-usable* physical region has been
26.    **reserved** (booked) — moved out of the free pool so a later `alloc()`
27.    can never hand it out;
28. 3. every **tracked** MMIO frame has been reserved, while MMIO frames the
29.    allocator does *not* track are **silently skipped** (coverage-gated);
30. 4. the **`PhysMemoryManager` singleton + a fresh user page pool are live**
31.    (the layer the rest of boot builds on);
32. 5. the whole thing satisfies the frame-allocator well-formedness
33.    `FrameAllocView::wf` (free/allocated disjoint, page-aligned,
34.    refcount-consistent).
35. 
36. `init` is the *only* externally observed function; `book_*` are private
37. helpers reachable only through `init`, so their contracts exist purely to
38. support `init`'s post-state. The caller observes **only `Ok(())` vs `Err`** —
39. never a partial state, never the iteration order, never the `Error` variant,
40. never whether MMIO is walked per-page.
41. 
42. These three functions are **free functions over global singletons**
43. (`frame::INSTANCE` + `frame::INSTANCE_INIT`, and the `PhysMemoryManager` /
44. `Upool` singletons), not `&mut self` methods. The View therefore models the
45. **abstract state of that global subsystem**, and the `v -> v'` transitions are
46. realized in the proof phase by a ghost token over the singletons (see §8) —
47. exactly as the bump-allocator View deferred its atomic-ghost token.
48. 
49. ---
50. 
51. ## 2. The View
52. 
53. The only abstract state these functions establish or mutate is: *is the
54. subsystem up*, *which physical frames are reserved vs. free*, and *is the
55. manager layer up*. The frame partition is **already** captured by the
56. do-not-modify `FrameAllocView` (the `View for Inner`). The phys-mod View wraps
57. it and adds the two liveness facts the caller depends on.
58. 
59. ```rust
60. /// Abstract view of the global physical-memory subsystem managed by
61. /// `mm::phys`. Pure ghost description — names no `MaybeUninit`, `AtomicBool`,
62. /// bitmap, refcount slice, or any other storage mechanism.
63. pub ghost struct PhysModView {
64.     /// The frame allocator singleton has been initialized (`frame::init` ran
65.     /// successfully). All `frames`-related guarantees are meaningful only
66.     /// when this holds.
67.     pub initialized: bool,
68.     /// Abstract frame-allocator state: which physical frames are allocated
69.     /// (reserved) vs. free, with per-frame refcounts. This is the existing,
70.     /// do-not-modify `FrameAllocView` (== the `View for Inner` of the global
71.     /// `frame::INSTANCE`).
72.     pub frames: FrameAllocView,
73.     /// The `PhysMemoryManager` singleton has been initialized with a fresh
74.     /// user page pool (`Upool`). A single liveness bit — the caller observes
75.     /// only that this layer is up, never its contents.
76.     pub manager_ready: bool,
77. }
78. ```
79. 
80. Attachment (no struct in `mod.rs` to `impl View` for; the state is global):
81. 
82. ```rust
83. /// Current abstract state of the global physical-memory subsystem.
84. /// Uninterpreted accessor; the proof phase pins it to the frame /
85. /// manager singletons via a ghost token (§8).
86. pub uninterp spec fn phys_view() -> PhysModView;
87. ```
88. 
89. `phys_view()` is read by specs exactly like `self@` would be: `init`'s ensures
90. talk about `phys_view()` before vs. after the call.
91. 
92. ### 2.1 Derived spec helpers
93. 
94. Reusable frame-set vocabulary lives **on `FrameAllocView`** (a *new* `impl`
95. block — the existing `struct`/`wf` are untouched), so every spec speaks the
96. same language:
97. 
98. ```rust
99. impl FrameAllocView {
100.     /// The allocator tracks (covers) the frame at `addr` — it is one of the
101.     /// frames this allocator knows about, allocated or free. Models
102.     /// `frame::is_covered`.
103.     pub open spec fn covers(self, addr: int) -> bool {
104.         self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) || self.free_frames.contains(addr)
105.     }
106. 
107.     /// The frame at `addr` is reserved: present in the allocated set, hence
108.     /// `alloc()` can never return it. This is the core caller-visible fact a
109.     /// "booked" frame satisfies.
110.     pub open spec fn reserved(self, addr: int) -> bool {
111.         self.allocated_frames.contains(addr)
112.     }
113. 
114.     /// Every frame address in `set` is reserved.
115.     pub open spec fn all_reserved(self, set: Set<int>) -> bool {
116.         forall|a: int| set.contains(a) ==> self.reserved(a)
117.     }
118. 
119.     /// Every frame address in `set` is currently free (booking precondition:
120.     /// a range can be booked only if it is entirely free).
121.     pub open spec fn all_free(self, set: Set<int>) -> bool {
122.         forall|a: int| set.contains(a) ==> self.free_frames.contains(a)
123.     }
124. }
125. ```
126. 
127. Region → frame-set bridge (defined over the public region accessors
128. `start()`/`size()`; exact closed form finalized in the spec phase):
129. 
130. ```rust
131. /// The set of page-aligned physical frame addresses covered by a physical
132. /// memory region `[start, start + size)`. Uses the existing `frame_addr_of`.
133. pub open spec fn region_frames(start_frame: int, num_frames: int) -> Set<int> {
134.     Set::new(|a: int| exists|i: int|
135.         0 <= i < num_frames && a == frame_addr_of(start_frame + i))
136. }
137. ```
138. 
139. PhysModView convenience predicate used in `init`'s post-state:
140. 
141. ```rust
142. impl PhysModView {
143.     /// The subsystem is fully brought up and self-consistent.
144.     pub open spec fn live(self) -> bool {
145.         self.initialized && self.manager_ready && self.frames.wf()
146.     }
147. }
148. ```
149. 
150. ---
151. 
152. ## 3. Well-formedness Invariant `inv()`
153. 
154. ```rust
155. impl PhysModView {
156.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
157.         // (a) Once the allocator is up, the frame partition is well formed.
158.         //     `FrameAllocView::wf` = free/allocated disjoint, page-aligned,
159.         //     refcount/allocated consistency, refcounts in 1..=255.
160.         &&& self.initialized ==> self.frames.wf()
161.         // (b) The manager layer is built on top of the frame allocator, so it
162.         //     can only be up if the allocator is up.
163.         &&& self.manager_ready ==> self.initialized
164.     }
165. }
166. ```
167. 
168. | Clause | Guarantees caller invariant |
169. |--------|-----------------------------|
170. | (a) `initialized ==> frames.wf()` | the downstream-relied-upon consistency (disjoint, aligned, refcount-consistent) holds whenever the allocator is live |
171. | (b) `manager_ready ==> initialized` | the manager singleton is never "up" over a dead allocator — rejects an init that builds the manager without seeding frames |
172. 
173. `inv()` is deliberately thin: the heavy lifting (`wf`) is reused from the
174. existing frame View, and the two implications encode the only ordering
175. constraint between the two liveness bits.
176. 
177. ---
178. 
179. ## 4. Spec transitions of the target functions
180. 
181. State is `v = phys_view()` (pre), `v' = phys_view()` (post). All clauses are
182. stated only over `PhysModView` / `FrameAllocView`; nothing names the
183. singleton storage.
184. 
185. ### 4.1 Frame-set transitions (on `FrameAllocView`)
186. 
187. ```rust
188. impl FrameAllocView {
189.     /// Reserve a single currently-free frame: move it from `free_frames` to
190.     /// `allocated_frames` with refcount 1. (Models `frame::book` /
191.     /// per-frame effect of `alloc_range` on a covered, free frame.)
192.     pub open spec fn book_frame(self, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
193.         FrameAllocView {
194.             allocated_frames: self.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
195.             free_frames: self.free_frames.remove(addr),
196.             refcounts: self.refcounts.insert(addr, 1),
197.         }
198.     }
199. 
200.     /// Reserve every frame in `set` (each must be free in `self`).
201.     /// Used to describe `alloc_range` over a region's frames.
202.     pub open spec fn book_all(self, set: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
203.         FrameAllocView {
204.             allocated_frames: self.allocated_frames.union(set),
205.             free_frames: self.free_frames.difference(set),
206.             refcounts: Map::new(
207.                 |a: int| self.refcounts.contains_key(a) || set.contains(a),
208.                 |a: int| if set.contains(a) { 1 } else { self.refcounts[a] }),
209.         }
210.     }
211. 
212.     /// Reserve only the *covered* frames of `set`; skip the rest (coverage-
213.     /// gated). Models the MMIO booking rule.
214.     pub open spec fn book_covered(self, set: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
215.         self.book_all(set.filter(|a: int| self.covers(a)))
216.     }
217. }
218. ```
219. 
220. ### 4.2 `book_physical_memory_regions(regions) -> Result<(), Error>`
221. 
222. Private; called once by `init`. Consumes the list by value. Let `R` be the
223. union of `region_frames(..)` over all regions in the list.
224. 
225. ```
226. requires  v.inv() && v.initialized          // allocator must be live first
227. 
228. ensures   v'.inv() && v'.initialized && v'.manager_ready == v.manager_ready
229. 
230.           match result {
231.             Ok(()) => {
232.               // every region was entirely free, and is now entirely reserved
233.               &&& v.frames.all_free(R)
234.               &&& v'.frames == v.frames.book_all(R)     // hence v'.frames.all_reserved(R)
235.             }
236.             Err(_) => {
237.               // fail-fast on a booking conflict: some region was NOT free.
238.               // Booking stops at the first failing region; earlier regions
239.               // stay booked, so the partition is still well formed but only a
240.               // prefix is reserved. No in-scope caller observes this state.
241.               &&& !v.frames.all_free(R)
242.               &&& v'.frames.wf()
243.             }
244.           }
245. ```
246. 
247. Error condition is stated as one **abstract interface predicate**
248. (`!all_free(R)` ⇔ a conflict with an already-reserved frame), not as a list of
249. code checks — this is the "fail-fast on conflict" property the caller relies on.
250. 
251. ### 4.3 `book_mmio_regions(&regions) -> Result<(), Error>`
252. 
253. Private; called once by `init`. Borrows the list. Let `M` be the union of
254. `region_frames(..)` over the MMIO regions (after GVA→GPA translation; the
255. translation is total on the success path).
256. 
257. ```
258. requires  v.inv() && v.initialized
259. 
260. ensures   v'.inv() && v'.initialized && v'.manager_ready == v.manager_ready
261. 
262.           match result {
263.             Ok(()) => {
264.               // tracked MMIO frames booked; untracked ones skipped, untouched.
265.               &&& v'.frames == v.frames.book_covered(M)
266.               // ⇒ forall f in M: v.frames.covers(f) ==> v'.frames.reserved(f)
267.               // ⇒ forall f in M: !v.frames.covers(f) ==> frame state unchanged
268.             }
269.             Err(_) => {
270.               // a covered frame was already reserved (book conflict) or an
271.               // address conversion failed; partition stays well formed.
272.               &&& v'.frames.wf()
273.             }
274.           }
275. ```
276. 
277. The `Ok` arm makes the coverage gate explicit and surfaces both halves the
278. caller depends on: covered ⇒ reserved, **and** uncovered ⇒ *not* assumed
279. reserved (state unchanged for those frames).
280. 
281. ### 4.4 `init(physical_memory_regions, &mmio_regions, physical_memory_layout) -> Result<(), Error>`
282. 
283. The only public function. Let `P` = union of `region_frames` over
284. `physical_memory_regions`, `M` = union over `mmio_regions`. `seed(bitmap)` is
285. the `FrameAllocView` produced by `frame::init` from the bitmap (frames it
286. tracks, partitioned per the bitmap's set bits).
287. 
288. ```
289. requires  v.inv()
290.           !v.initialized            // one-shot: frame allocator not yet up
291.                                      // (frame::init rejects a second call)
292. 
293. ensures   v'.inv()
294. 
295.           match result {
296.             Ok(()) => {
297.               // (1) subsystem fully live & consistent
298.               &&& v'.live()                          // initialized && manager_ready && frames.wf()
299.               // (2) seeded from the bitmap, then phys regions booked, then
300.               //     covered MMIO frames booked
301.               &&& v'.frames == seed(physical_memory_layout@)
302.                                    .book_all(P)
303.                                    .book_covered(M)
304.               // (3) booked ⇒ never allocated (the core safety property)
305.               &&& v'.frames.all_reserved(P)
306.               &&& forall|f: int| M.contains(f) && v'.frames.covers(f)
307.                       ==> v'.frames.reserved(f)
308.             }
309.             Err(_) => {
310.               // boot aborts; caller uses `?` and never touches the subsystem
311.               // again. No partial-state guarantee is promised beyond inv().
312.               true
313.             }
314.           }
315. ```
316. 
317. Notes:
318. - (1) `v'.live()` is the single fact downstream `virt::init` / page-table
319.   setup needs (both singletons up, `wf` holds). It rejects a buggy `init`
320.   that returns `Ok` while leaving a singleton uninitialized.
321. - (3) is the headline caller property ("booked ⇒ never allocated"); it is
322.   *derivable* from (2) (`book_all`/`book_covered` definitions) but surfaced
323.   directly because it is exactly what the caller writes into its proof.
324. - The `Err` arm is intentionally `true` (only `inv()` is promised): the caller
325.   aborts on `?` and the analysis states no in-scope caller observes any
326.   particular partial state. Strengthening it would over-specify an
327.   unobserved, non-transactional path.
328. 
329. ---
330. 
331. ## 5. Substitution test (per field)
332. 
333. > *"If `mm::phys` / the frame allocator were rewritten with a different
334. > algorithm (e.g. a buddy allocator, a free-list, a different singleton
335. > mechanism), would this field still make sense?"*
336. 
337. | Field | Survives? | Reasoning |
338. |-------|-----------|-----------|
339. | `initialized` | ✅ | "Is the physical-memory subsystem up?" is observable regardless of how the singleton is stored (`AtomicBool`, `OnceCell`, …). The caller depends on exactly this one-shot liveness. |
340. | `frames: FrameAllocView` | ✅ | The free/allocated/refcount partition is the abstract resource *any* frame allocator maintains; it is the existing `View for Inner`. A buddy/free-list rewrite still exposes the same `Set<int>` partition. Names no bitmap/refcount-slice. |
341. | `manager_ready` | ✅ | "Is the `PhysMemoryManager` + user page pool layer up?" is a caller-observable liveness bit independent of how the manager is built. A single bool — the caller observes liveness, never contents. |
342. 
343. Every field describes the **subsystem's observable state**, not a mechanism.
344. The implementation's `MaybeUninit<Inner>`, `AtomicBool`, `Bitmap`, and
345. `[u8; NFRAMES]` refcount storage are *one* realization; the View commits to
346. none of them.
347. 
348. Helper predicates pass too: `covers`/`reserved`/`book_*` are phrased over the
349. abstract frame sets (`is_covered` = "tracked", `book` = "move free→allocated"),
350. all algorithm-independent.
351. 
352. ---
353. 
354. ## 6. Design rationale
355. 
356. - **Reuse, don't re-derive, the frame partition.** `FrameAllocView` already is
357.   the correct abstract state for the allocator and is shared with the
358.   `frame` submodule's verified `View for Inner`. Embedding it (rather than
359.   re-modeling frames) keeps `init`/`book_*` specs interoperable with the
360.   frame-level contracts they call (`frame::book`, `frame::alloc_range`,
361.   `frame::is_covered`) and honors the do-not-modify constraint.
362. - **Two liveness bits, nothing more.** The caller's *additional* observations
363.   beyond the frame partition are exactly "allocator up" and "manager up". Each
364.   is a single bool, each is used (`initialized` gates `book_*` preconditions
365.   and `frames.wf()`; `manager_ready` appears in `init`'s `live()`
366.   post-state). Minimal and complete.
367. - **Coverage-gating modeled as a `filter`.** `book_covered = book_all ∘
368.   filter(covers)` makes "tracked ⇒ booked, untracked ⇒ skipped" one
369.   declarative line, capturing the LAPIC-above-RAM skip the caller is warned
370.   about — without walking GVA→GPA per page.
371. - **Reserve-set vocabulary on the View.** `reserved`/`all_reserved`/`all_free`
372.   + `region_frames` turn "booked ⇒ never allocated" and the booking
373.   precondition into reusable predicates, so each ensures is a clause a caller
374.   drops straight into a proof.
375. - **Error paths fold to `inv()` (+ a conflict predicate).** Booking is
376.   non-transactional (partial on failure) and no in-scope caller observes the
377.   partial state, so the honest contract is: `Err` preserves `wf` and (for
378.   `book_physical_memory_regions`) reveals the abstract conflict condition
379.   `!all_free(R)`. We do **not** fabricate state-preservation that the code
380.   does not provide.
381. - **`init` post-state as a composed transition.** `seed(..).book_all(P)
382.   .book_covered(M)` is a single declarative description of the whole boot
383.   sequence; the headline safety fact (3) is surfaced separately because that
384.   is the form the caller actually uses.
385. 
386. ---
387. 
388. ## 7. Rejected alternatives
389. 
390. 1. **No phys-mod View; specs reference `FrameAllocView` (and the raw global)
391.    directly.** Rejected. The frame partition alone cannot express "the
392.    allocator is initialized" (one-shot `init` precondition) or "the manager
393.    layer is up" — both are caller-observed. A thin wrapper carrying the two
394.    liveness bits is the minimal honest model.
395. 
396. 2. **Mirror the implementation: fields `instance_init: bool`,
397.    `bitmap: Seq<bool>`, `refcount: Seq<u8>`.** Rejected. Leaks the
398.    `AtomicBool` + `Bitmap` + refcount-slice mechanism, fails the substitution
399.    test (a buddy/free-list rewrite has no bitmap), and duplicates state the
400.    existing `FrameAllocView` already abstracts.
401. 
402. 3. **Model the manager/Upool with a full sub-View
403.    (`manager: PhysMemoryManagerView`).** Rejected for *this* module. The
404.    in-scope functions only need "manager up" (one bit); the caller observes
405.    only liveness here. A structured manager View belongs to the `manager`
406.    module's own verification, not phys-mod, and would require reading its
407.    internals (forbidden, and unnecessary). Promote to a sub-View later only if
408.    a caller is shown to depend on manager contents.
409. 
410. 4. **Track per-region booking results / fault flags in the View.** Rejected.
411.    Errors are transient return values the caller maps to abort-on-`?`; no error
412.    is part of the persistent abstract resource. Conflict conditions live in
413.    per-call `ensures` (`!all_free(R)`), not in `PhysModView`.
414. 
415. 5. **Make the `Err` arm of `init`/`book_*` promise full state preservation
416.    (`v' == v`).** Rejected as unsound: booking mutates the global incrementally
417.    and stops at the first conflict, so earlier regions stay booked. The code
418.    does not roll back; a `v' == v` ensures would be a false spec. We promise
419.    only `inv()` (and the conflict predicate), which is all any caller observes.
420. 
421. 6. **Represent reserved frames as a `Seq<int>` (ordered) instead of reusing
422.    `Set<int>` from `FrameAllocView`.** Rejected. Order of booking is explicitly
423.    *not* caller-observable (the analysis lists "ordering in which regions are
424.    iterated" as a non-breaking internal). Sets are the right abstraction and
425.    are already the established frame-View vocabulary.
426. 
427. ---
428. 
429. ## 8. Global-state modeling note (deferred to proof phase)
430. 
431. `init`/`book_*` take **no `self`**: they read and mutate the global singletons
432. `frame::INSTANCE` (+ `INSTANCE_INIT`) and the `PhysMemoryManager`/`Upool`
433. singletons. The `v -> v'` transitions in §4 are therefore not a literal
434. `old(self)`/`self` pair. They will be realized in the proof phase by a ghost
435. token whose invariant is exactly `PhysModView::inv()` and whose value is
436. `PhysModView`, with:
437. 
438. - `initialized`  ↔ `frame::INSTANCE_INIT`,
439. - `frames`       ↔ `frame::INSTANCE@` (the verified `View for Inner`, valid when
440.   `initialized`),
441. - `manager_ready`↔ the `PhysMemoryManager` singleton's init flag.
442. 
443. This is an *attachment* detail; the abstract View, `inv()`, and the transitions
444. above are the target the token machinery must satisfy and do not change. (Same
445. pattern the bump-allocator View used to defer its atomic-ghost token.)
446.

description: "How to write good Verus specs. Covers spec quality principles (anti-patterns, error paths), spec classification (internal, external-top, external-bottom trust boundaries), View abstraction design, and static vs dynamic enforcement. Use when writing or reviewing Verus specs."
---

# Spec Design Guide

## Part 1: Spec Quality Principles

### Qualities of a Good Spec

1. **Bound to exec code** — every property must appear as `requires`,
   `ensures`, or loop `invariant` on an exec function. Standalone spec
   functions that no exec function references prove nothing.
2. **Annotates the original** — specs are added directly to the original
   exec function using `#[verus_spec]` (see `verus-syntax` skill). Never
   copy exec functions into a `verus!{}` block and spec the copy — that
   verifies the copy, not the real code.
3. **Sufficient to reject bugs** — if you can imagine a buggy implementation
   that still satisfies the spec, the spec is incomplete. A sorting spec
   that omits `is_sorted` passes a function that just copies the input.
4. **Declarative, not operational** — a spec describes **what** must be true,
   not **how** the code achieves it. If you could swap quicksort for
   bubblesort and the spec still makes sense, it's a good spec.
5. **Simpler than the code** — the spec should be at a higher level of
   abstraction than the implementation. For example, where the code has
   loops, the spec may use `forall`, `Seq`/`Set`/`Map` operations, or
   recursive spec functions.
6. **Independent from the code** — two independent statements of the same truth.
   If derived by reading code line-by-line, it will reproduce bugs. A useful
   test: **could you have written this spec from just the function signature,
   type definitions, and module purpose — without reading the implementation?**
   If not, the spec likely mirrors the code rather than abstracting over it.
7. **Uses mathematical objects where they simplify reasoning** — prefer `int`
   over `u32`/`i32` (avoids overflow in specs), `Seq`/`Set`/`Map` over
   `Vec`/`HashMap`. Use `view()` / `self@` for abstract state. For pointer
   addresses, prefer `usize` over `int` — addresses are inherently
   non-negative and bounded by the address space.
8. **Written for the caller** — for each ensures clause, simulate
   writing a caller's proof that uses this function. Would you use
   this fact as-is, or would you need to transform, combine, or
   unwrap it first? A good ensures clause is one the caller writes
   directly into their proof. Prefer vstd's existing spec functions
   (e.g., `self@.contains(x)`) over manual encodings (e.g.,
   `exists|i| ... && self@[i] == x`) — callers already reason with
   vstd APIs. On `exists`: valid when it genuinely hides
   implementation choice, but if the witness is computable from inputs

# Verus Constraints

## Attribute Style for Exec Functions

All specs on **exec functions** must use the attribute-based syntax
(`#[verus_spec]`, `#[verus_verify]`, `proof! { }`, `proof_decl! { }`).
See the **verus-syntax** skill for the full reference and examples.

```rust
// ✅ CORRECT — attribute style for exec functions
#[verus_spec(ret =>
    requires x < 100,
    ensures ret == x + 1,
)]
fn foo(x: u32) -> u32 {
    x + 1
}

// ❌ WRONG — do not wrap exec functions in verus! { }
verus! {
    fn foo(x: u32) -> (ret: u32)
        requires x < 100,
        ensures ret == x + 1,
    { x + 1 }
} // verus!
```

**`verus! { }` blocks** are still used for:
- `spec fn` and `proof fn` definitions (in `.spec.rs` and `.proof.rs`)
- Type-level specs (`broadcast`, `impl View`, etc.)

Key benefit: exec function signatures stay unmodified — the original `fn`
signature is untouched, specs live in the attribute.

## Source Integrity (exec code)

The following rules apply to the original source files (e.g. `lib.rs`), not to
`*.spec.rs` / `*.proof.rs` which are freely editable.

Verus verification is **in-place**: specs and proofs are added directly alongside
exec code. The annotated code remains fully compilable and runnable — Verus
constructs are erased during normal `cargo build` via cfg-gating. Keep changes
minimal so developers can review diffs easily.

**Preserve by default:** exec logic, function signatures, struct definitions,
comments, debug assertions, and all other existing code.

The escalation ladder (each step requires exhausting the previous):

1. **Verify as-is** — most code works with Verus directly.
2. **Search vstd** — your training data is likely outdated. `grep -r` the entire
   vstd directory broadly (see "vstd & Common Misconceptions" section below).
3. If verification still fails after steps 1–2, try different proof
   strategies (add lemmas, intermediate assertions, split into smaller
   functions). If Verus reports that a **syntax construct is unsupported**
   (not a proof failure and not a missing spec for a stdlib function),
   record it in `verus-unsupported.md` with the exact error message and
   the minimal code that triggers it. Do NOT rewrite exec code, add
   `external_body`, or add `assume_specification` to work around it.

**The exec code has been pre-refactored to be fully compatible with Verus.**
There are no known Verus front-end limitations in the codebase. Any
verification failure is a proof issue, not a Verus limitation. Do NOT
rewrite exec code, add `external_body` — these are never needed.

**Never cfg-gate away and duplicate exec definitions.** Adding
`#[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]` to a function, impl block, struct, enum, or
constant and providing a verus-annotated copy is forbidden — it verifies the
copy, not the real code, and the two will silently diverge.

- **Functions / impl blocks**: add contracts to the original in-place.
- **Structs / enums**: Verus sees the original definition directly. If a
  derive macro is incompatible, cfg-gate only the derive attribute, not
  the struct. If the struct truly cannot be parsed by Verus, use
  `external_type_specification` in spec.rs to declare it — do not
  duplicate the definition. Write `external_type_specification` **once**
  in the crate/module that defines the type; other modules `use` it.
- **Constants**: Verus sees the original definition directly. If Verus
  cannot resolve a constant from another workspace module, add
  `#[verus_verify]` to the defining module. Never
  `#[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]` the original constant.

**Allowed additions:** `#[verus_spec(...)]` and `#[verus_verify]` attributes,
`proof! { }` / `proof_decl! { }` / `proof_with! { }` macros, `#[verus_spec(...)]`
on loops, `verus! { }` blocks (for spec/proof fn in .spec.rs/.proof.rs),
vstd imports (cfg-gated), ghost/tracked local variables (each must be
used by at least one proof construct — assertion, invariant, or proof block),
`Ghost<T>` / `Tracked<T>` struct fields (only when proof requires ghost
state to flow through exec code — prefer keeping ghost state in View),
`#[cfg_attr(not(verus_keep_ghost), derive(...))]` gating.

**After completing all changes**, use the `ast-consistency` skill to verify
source integrity. Fix all inconsistencies.

## Forbidden Patterns

| Pattern | Policy |
|---|---|
| `admit()` | Allowed during specification phase as a placeholder. Must be eliminated during proving phase |
| `assume(...)` | Banned |
| `#[verifier::external_body]` | **On current module's own functions**: unconditionally forbidden in all phases — `admit()` in a proof body is the correct placeholder during specification (it skips only the proof obligation while Verus still checks exec code; `external_body` skips everything). **On dependency functions in other modules**: allowed as a temporary contract placeholder while the dependency is not yet verified. Must be removed when the dependency module is verified |
| `#[verifier::trusted]` | Banned |
| `#[verifier::external]` | Banned — not needed under attribute style (only `#[verus_verify]`-annotated items are checked) |
| `#[verifier::exec_allows_no_decreases_clause]` | Banned |
